title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Emerald Herald -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : The Emerald Herald's real name is Shanalotte, a name given to her by the dragons. Born of dragons but contrived by men, she was created specifically to break the undead curse, but her creators failed and she did not come out as intended. Despite this, she guides undead towards the Throne of Want, waiting for a powerful undead that might defeat the Four Old Ones, succeed Vendrick and end the undead curse.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet: Royal Sorcerer Navlaan tells the player many people believe the Emerald Herald is the last firekeeper. Navlaan will also say she is sometimes known as the "Muse".

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Emerald Herald -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : The Emerald Herald was originally featured in the first trailer for *Dark Souls II*, where she is seen overlooking Drangleic and gives a feather to the Bearer of the Curse.
Her mixed and unusual heritage is evidenced by her eyes. She has complete *heterochromia iridum*: her left eye is brown, while her right eye, which is hidden by her hair, is purple. The only way to view this is to move so that the camera can clip through her model.
While a child model of the Emerald Herald does exist within the games files, there is no dialogue showing what purpose the child version would have served.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Emerald Herald -  Dark Souls II - character - lead 
 lead : The **Emerald Herald** is a character in *Dark Souls II*. She is voiced by Ruth Negga.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - dragon_aerie 
 dragon_aerie : Following the symbol of the King will lead the Bearer of the Curse to Aldia's Keep. Aldia was the King's brother, who sought to create dragons, and has long since disappeared. Journeying through the Keep, home to the results of Aldia's mad experiments, will eventually bring the Bearer to the Dragon Aerie, where they will find the Emerald Herald awaiting them. She directs the Bearer to the very top of the Aerie, the Dragon Shrine, to seek the Ancient Dragon. She claims that the dragon has been watching over the world for aeons, and awaits the Bearer of the Curse.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Emerald Herald -  Dark Souls II - character - plot 
 plot : Much like the Maiden in Black from *Demon's Souls*, the Emerald Herald serves as the player's means of leveling up, replacing the bonfires of *Dark Souls* in this respect.

She gives the player an Estus Flask upon introducing herself. Bringing her Estus Flask Shards will increase the total amount of charges that the Flask can hold.

She gives the player the Aged Feather when spoken to upon arrival in Dragon Aerie.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - throne_of_want 
 throne_of_want : Below Drangleic Castle, the Throne of Want awaits. Here the Emerald Herald will meet the Bearer of the Curse one final time, declaring her journey completed. She warns that if the Bearer of the Curse proceeds, Nashandra, knowing the Bearer of the Curse will link the fire, and coveting the power of the First Flame and the Great Soul, will come for them. She urges the Bearer of the Curse to put an end to Nashandra.

After defeating the Throne Watcher and Defender, the Bearer of the Curse will be greeted by Nashandra, now in her true form, as a child of Manus, Father of the Abyss. The Bearer of the Curse defeats Nashandra.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
The Bearer of the Curse fights their way through the knights and defeats Velstadt, finding Vendrick at last. The King, however, has been reduced to a hollow, wandering the grounds aimlessly. The Bearer may choose to put the king out of his misery, or leave him to wander endlessly. Here, the Bearer of the Curse finds the King's Ring, and the Emerald Herald, who tells them that the ring will open the way to the far east, where the Bearer of the Curse must journey next. She proceeds to warn the Bearer that if they continue on this path, they too will one day walk these grounds without really remembering why.

Should the Bearer of the Curse seek her council, Nashandra too will direct the Bearer of the Curse to follow the symbol of the King.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - prologue 
 prologue : The Bearer of the Curse became undead at some point, hollowing until they had no recollection of their former life. Desperate to find a cure, they were drawn to the walled off kingdom of Drangleic, where a cure to the undead curse was rumored to exist. Journeying through a portal and guided by a Fire Keeper, the Bearer of the Curse found themselves in the Things Betwixt. Finding there a hut with the remaining Fire Keepers, the Bearer of the Curse is made to remember more of their past and is cured of their hollowing through a Human Effigy. The Bearer is then guided towards Majula to seek the Emerald Herald.

The Herald, in turn, tells the Bearer of the Curse to seek the king, Vendrick, to find their answers and claim the throne, but warns that the Bearer will never find the king with a soul so pallid, instructing them to seek out the four Great Ones and to claim their power.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Emerald Herald -  Dark Souls II - character - strategy 
 strategy : If the player lowers her health down to half, she will refuse to talk and will simply stand still. Resting at a bonfire will reset her health to normal, but she will still ignore the player until they have spoken with Cromwell the Pardoner.

She drops the Aged Feather if killed.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - lead 
 lead : The **Bearer of the Curse** is the player character and the protagonist of *Dark Souls II* and its expansions, *The Lost Crowns*.

The Bearer of the Curse travels to Drangleic by a compulsion to find a way to break the curse of the undead and avoid Hollowing at any cost.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - four_great_ones 
 four_great_ones : The Bearer of the Curse sets out to find the Four Great Ones.

Through the rotunda in Majula, the Bearer of the Curse makes their way to the ancient domain of the Old Iron King, whose hubris led to his death beneath the molten iron, where he was possessed by the soul of one whose name must not be repeated. Making their way through the king's old hunting grounds and the now poison-filled valley surrounding the castle, the Bearer of the Curse finds and slays the Old Iron King, claiming his soul for their own.

By way of ship or on the wings of an eagle, the Bearer of the Curse makes their way to The Lost Bastille, a forgotten prison where the Lost Sinner is held. The Lost Sinner was imprisoned for the sin of attempting to relight the First Flame. The Bearer of the Curse fights their way down into the very bottom of the prison, where they face the Sinner and take her soul for their own.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - drangleic_castle 
 drangleic_castle : Now with the strength of the four Great Ones, the Bearer of the Curse may pass through the Shrine of Winter to reach Drangleic Castle, the stronghold of Vendrick himself. The Emerald Herald awaits outside, directing the Bearer of the Curse to enter the castle. There is no trace of the King inside the castle however, instead the Bearer of the Curse finds his Queen, Nashandra. Nashandra tells the Bearer of the Curse that Vendrick was less of a king than one might imagine, and that he never took the true throne. She will direct the Bearer of the Curse to the Undead Crypt, to put an end to Vendrick.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Shanalotte will once again appear once the Bearer of the Curse has reached the Dragon Aerie. Here, she will reveal that it was her manifestations that led them here, and has been guiding them all along. She directs the Bearer to the top of the aerie, where the Ancient Dragon awaits them.

Shanalotte will appear one final time when the Bearer of the Curse is approaching the Throne of Want. She will tell the Bearer of her origins and her true name. She will warn them that Nashandra, desiring the power of the Flame and the Great Soul will come after them, but that they must persist nonetheless.

Should the Bearer of the Curse choose to claim the throne, Shanalotte will narrate their ascent, explaining that linking the flame will cause souls to flourish anew but that the events that have transpired will play out all over again, and that it is the Bearer's choice whether to embrace or renounce this.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Once arriving at the Dragon Shrine bonfire, the Scholar appears once more. He will reveal that he is in fact Aldia, the elder brother of Vendrick. Aldia says that he "sought to shed the yoke of fate, but failed" and that he now only awaits an answer. He asks of the Bearer of the Curse to "seek the Throne, seek light, dark and what lies beyond", for the last time, he'll vanish into the flames, allowing the Bearer of the Curse to light the bonfire.

The Ancient Dragon will give the Bearer the Ashen Mist Heart, which allows one to peer into the memories of things long withered. Should the Bearer of the Curse again seek out Nashandra's council, she will warn that the dragon is a false deity and is in fact no more than a prop. Still, she will direct the Bearer of the Curse to go to the Forest of Fallen Giants, to use the Ashen Mist Heart to peer into the Giants' memories.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Finally, the Bearer of the Curse travels to Frozen Eleum Loyce, once ruled by the Ivory King. Built to contain the Old Chaos, the city was abandoned and froze over when its king vanished into the chaos. Guided by the last child of the Abyss, Alsanna, Silent Oracle, the Bearer of the Curse seeks out the remaining knights of Eleum Loyce to gain their help in braving the Old Chaos. Finding the Burnt Ivory King there, the Bearer of the Curse defeats him and claims his crown.

Once the Bearer of the Curse has found all three crowns of old, along with Vendrick's own crown, the fallen king will unleash the hidden power of the crowns, making the Bearer of the Curse immune to the hollowing effects of the curse. Bidding the Bearer to seek strength, and asking them whether allowing the flames to fade is truly their only choice, the king sends the Bearer of the Curse on their way.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet: If Vendrick is defeated before Nashandra, and the Bearer of the Curse has spoken to Aldia in the three mentioned locations, answering yes to both questions asked by Aldia, after Nashandra's defeat, Aldia will appear saying that "many monarchs have come and gone" and requires the Bearer of the Curse's answer as "conqueror of adversities". Aldia will then test the Bearer of the Curse to see if they are truly worthy of receiving the throne by confronting them himself. The Bearer of the Curse defeats Aldia. After Aldia, The Scholar of the First Sin is defeated, the Bearer of the Curse is given two endings.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
She eventually finds this someone in the Bearer of the Curse, an undead with no memory of their origins from a far away land. Shanalotte guides the Bearer of the Curse in their quest, telling them to seek souls and to seek the king. She will guide the Bearer of the Curse to seek out the Four Old Ones in order to claim their powerful souls. Once the Bearer of the Curse has done this, the way to Drangleic Castle, the home of Vendrick, will be open. Shanalotte will wait outside the castle, directing the Bearer of the Curse to enter.

She will next appear in the Undead Crypt, where Vendrick now wanders aimlessly. After the Bearer of the Curse has claimed the king's ring, she will direct them to follow the mark of the king and journey east, and warn them that if they continue on this path, they too will one day walk these same grounds, without really knowing why.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet: When about to light the last primal bonfire, the Bearer of the Curse is surprised by the Scholar of the First Sin, who emerges from the bonfire. The Scholar asks if they want to "shed the curse", unless they have already joined the crestfallen, he tells them that there are two paths: to inherit the order of the world, or destroy it. He admits that very few have come this far, and yet the Bearer's journey is far from over. The Scholar asks of the Bearer to seek Vendrick, "he who almost became a true monarch", for he will guide their way. After this, the Scholar will disappear, letting the Bearer of the Curse light the primal bonfire.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - undead_crypt 
 undead_crypt : After traveling through the Shrine of Amana, the Bearer of the Curse will come upon the Undead Crypt, a place that has stood since the dawn of time, and where men and gods alike have been interred. Here, Vendrick came along with his loyal knights and his right hand, Velstadt, the Royal Aegis. Many servants of Vendrick have come to find the King, only to meet their end at the hands of the Royal Aegis and the King's knights.

Upon descending from the elevator, the Bearer of the Curse will stumble upon the Scholar once more if met at the last primal bonfire. The Scholar will ask the Bearer if they still desire peace, if answered yes, he will tell them that Vendrick is here and not far off. He will state that the Bearer was neither born with greatness nor granted it by the fates, before once again disappearing into the flames.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
The Bearer of the Curse will journey through the Black Gulch to find the fallen kingdom of Shulva, Sanctum City, once ruled by the Sunken King. The king ruled the city, centred around the worship of a slumbering dragon known as Sinh, until his kingdom was invaded by the Drakeblood Knights lead by Sir Yorgh, who sought to claim the dragon's blood. Sir Yorgh slew the king, and awoke the dragon, which proceeded to kill him and lay waste to the city with its poison. The Bearer of the Curse slays Elana, the Squalid Queen, a child of the Abyss, and the dragon Sinh to claim the Sunken King's crown.

Next, the Bearer of the Curse returns to the Old Iron Kingdom, to seek the Old Iron King's crown. Finding the kingdom under the sway of another child of the Abyss, Nadalia, Bride of Ash, the Bearer braves their way through the ruined towers to find the Fume Knight, who guards the crown of the Old Iron King.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - giant_memories 
 giant_memories : Using the Ashen Mist Heart on the corpse of the giant Jeigh will allow the Bearer of the Curse to enter the giant's memories and fight the Giant Lord during the final days of the war between Drangleic and the Giants. Upon defeating the Giant Lord, they will acquire the Giant's Kinship which will allow them to claim the Throne of Want.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - the_three_crowns 
 the_three_crowns : Should the Bearer of the Curse choose to do so, they may use the Ashen Mist Heart on Vendrick's belongings in the Undead Crypt. Doing so will allow the Bearer to speak directly to the king as he was before he hollowed. Bitter and resigned to defeat, the king will council the Bearer of the Curse, warning them of the futility in seeking fire, of the dark that lies within them, and of the children of Manus, Father of the Abyss. He will tell the Bearer to seek three crowns of power, belonging to fallen kings. He will also warn the Bearer of his wife, Nashandra, revealing that she too is a child of the Abyss.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - epilogue 
 epilogue : ***Proceed to the Throne:** In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse will accept their part in the cycle of the world, and take the throne. Doing so means that they will either sacrifice themselves to link the flame, or allow the flame to continue fading and become the Dark Lord. Which the Bearer of the Curse chooses is unknown.

***Leave the Throne: **In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse rejects the throne, and bitterly walks away, seemingly to seek another, more permanent way to end the curse.

title: Old Ones
snippet: The four current owners of the Great Souls as of the Bearer of the Curse’s arrival in Drangleic are the Old Iron King, the Lost Sinner, The Rotten and The Duke's Dear Freja. The Emerald Herald instructs the Bearer of the Curse to acquire the Great Souls to gain their power and use them as a beacon to reach Vendrick.

title: Fire Keeper
snippet: All Fire Keepers in the series suffer substantial ailments: Anastacia has neither tongue nor feet, Quelaag's Sister is gravely ill in addition to being twisted by the Flame of Chaos, and the Darkmoon Knightess has a "ghastly form" and "hideous swarms of humanity" hidden under her armor, while the unnamed *Dark Souls III* Fire Keeper, seemingly all of her Lothric predecessors, the Old Ladies, and Irina are all blind. The Emerald Herald, who might be a Keeper, has no visible affliction, although she claims that she "did not come out as intended".

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Once the Bearer of the Curse has finally cleared the way to the Throne and acquired the means to access it, Nashandra will intercept them and reveal her true form. She then declares the Bearer of the Curse worthy to assume her intended role for Vendrick, to have their power usurped by her so she can claim the throne for herself.

The Bearer of the Curse has grown too strong however, and Nashandra falls at their hand.

title: Crestfallen Saulden
snippet:
Despite his pessimistic outlook on life and existence, he still has much faith in the Way of Blue, a humble religion spread among those who seek help. He seems to have been a follower even before his loss of will, since the Emerald Herald describes him as a "blue knight". He will let the Bearer of the Curse join the covenant if they ever feel overwhelmed and in need of assistance.

The Bearer of the Curse can eventually lead more people to Majula, which will lighten Saulden's mood and make him remember better times. Finding new peace in companionship, he'll feel gratitude towards the adventurer.

title: Royal Sorcerer Navlaan
snippet: Navlaan is discovered in his prison by the Bearer of the Curse. If the Bearer is hollow, the malevolent entity will speak them, asking them to perform a series of murders and to bring Navlaan proof of their victims' demise, in return for rewards. These victims are Laddersmith Gilligan, Cale the Cartographer, Felkin the Outcast, and finally, the Emerald Herald. His first two targets appear to have angered Navlaan in some way, in particular Cale, who came upon Navlaan in his travels and treated him as if he were a rare species of animal. His reasons for wishing Felkin dead are unknown, and he requests that the Bearer kills the Emerald Herald because he wants them to kill "someone of import", though he expresses doubt in her claims to be the "Last Firekeeper".

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Her appearance and background resemble those of the character Lady Oscar from The Rose of Versailles (ベルサイユのばら) by Riyoko Ikeda.
The description of Lucatiel's Mask in Dark Souls III mentions Lucatiel and the Bearer of the Curse, implying that the Bearer kept their promise to remember her name.

title: Royal Sorcerer Navlaan
snippet: The Bearer of the Curse may either assassinate Navlaan's targets, or acquire the proof Navlaan seeks through peaceful means, allowing them to trick him into believing his marks are dead. Either way, Navlaan will be at peace, and offer his services as a merchant. If the Bearer of the Curse releases Navlaan, Navlaan will declare that he has found a new mark, and will begin relentlessly pursuing them.

title: Magerold of Lanafir
snippet: Magerold also displays a fascination with dragons, secretly being an adherent of the Dragon Remnants and seeking the location of the Dragon Shrine so he may find great treasures there. The Bearer of the Curse can bring him one such artifact, a mysterious stone egg, likely that of a dragon. Upon being given the fine specimen, he will allow the adventurer into his covenant.

title: Aged Feather
snippet:
Aged Feather -  Dark Souls II - item - trivia 
 trivia : The Emerald Herald uses the Aged Feather to level up the player's character. The player cannot use it for this purpose, though.
The name of the item was changed to *Feather of Estentia* post patch 1.08 in the Spanish version of the game.

title: Carhillion of the Fold
snippet: If he finds an apprentice he'll return to Majula, where he will also meet back with Rosabeth, who decided to walk her own path in the meantime. However, seeking answers seems to lead him to Brume Tower as well, perhaps sensing the dark power of Nadalia, Bride of Ash. There he'll aid the Bearer of the Curse in taking down the Fume Knight should they summon him. During the fight it's revealed the old sorcerer has dabbled into Hexing while in Drangleic, something he wouldn't be able to do in most lands, as they view the art as an affront to life itself.

title: Dragon
snippet: The Ancient Dragon residing in the Dragon Shrine is said by the Emerald Herald to have watched over the world for "aeons". However, the veracity of this is doubtful, and he may have been resurrected by Lord Aldia instead of being a survivor from the War of Fire, since Aldia attempted to recreate the dragons using giant souls. The former is far more likely as when the Ancient Dragon is slain, the Bearer of the Curse receives a Giant Soul. He gifts the Ashen Mist Heart, a manifestation of ashen mist whose magic can allow one to delve into the memories of the long-deceased, such as dead Giants and even a Dragon, as well as to pull items and souls from those memories into the real world. Whether this is an actual magic of the Dragons that the Ancient Dragon's body manages to inherit is unknown, but it remains doubtful since the Ancient Dragon may be a false Dragon.

title: King's Ring
snippet:
King's Ring -  Dark Souls II - ring - trivia 
 trivia : If the player positions the camera towards the entrance at the top of the stairs, they will see the Emerald Herald suddenly appear as soon as they pick up the ring.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Bearer of the Curse: A human who ended up in Drangleic in search of a solution for the curse of Undeath, overcame multiple challenges and gathered powerful souls before gaining access to the Throne of Want.

title: The Pursuer
snippet:
The Pursuer -  Dark Souls II - boss - description 
 description : The Pursuer is a mysterious figure who relentlessly hunts the Bearer of the Curse. The Pursuer tracks the Bearer to the Forest of Fallen Giants, The Lost Bastille, the Iron Keep and lastly Drangleic Castle.

title: Undead
snippet: The sudden appearance of the Curse among the human population is seemingly connected to the waning state of the First Flame, though it is unclear why some humans are affected while others are not. The Chosen Undead in *Dark Souls* and the Bearer of the Curse in *Dark Souls II* are both Undead, while The Ashen One in *Dark Souls III* is Unkindled, possessing a similar yet distinct form of Undeath which does not result in Hollowing.

title: Nashandra
snippet: Left without a king and with no means to claim the Throne of Want, Nashandra’s plans were stalled until the arrival of the Bearer of the Curse, an undead powerful enough to defeat the Four Old Ones and gain access to Drangleic Castle. Nashandra manipulated the Bearer of the Curse into opening the way to the Throne of Want by aiding them in seizing the Throne of Want. She directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Undead Crypt, suggesting that they put an end to the now-hollowed King Vendrick and claim his ring. She then directs the Bearer of the Curse to journey to Aldia's Keep to acquire the Ashen Mist Heart, and warns them that the Ancient Dragon there is no more than a prop and a false deity. At last, she directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Forest of Fallen Giants to visit the memories of the Giants and obtain the last key to the Throne: the Giant's Kinship.

title: Herald Helm
snippet:
Herald Helm -  Dark Souls III - armor - lead 
 lead : The **Herald Helm** is a head armor piece in *Dark Souls III*. It is part of the Herald Set.

title: Fire Keeper
snippet:
In *Dark Souls II*, the three Fire Keepers in Things Betwixt and the Emerald Herald, believed by some to be Fire Keeper, can be killed without the nearby bonfire being affected. The way the Herald can level up the Bearer of the Curse is reminescent of how the Fire Keepers in *Dark Souls III* can the Ashen One. One of the Keepers, Strowen, offers the player to re-allocate their attributes in exchange for a Soul Vessel.

In *Dark Souls III*, the unnamed Fire Keeper can level up the Ashen One like the Hemerald did in the previous game. She is also immortal; killing her, in addition to not causing the Shrine bonfire to be affected, will only cause her to respawn upon reloading the area, claiming that she cannot die. Instead of a Keeper, it is Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth, the leader of the Rosaria's Fingers covenant, who allows the player to re-allocate their attributes.

title: Fire Keeper

Little is known about Yoel besides the fact that he is a pilgrim and was once a sorcerer. However, he also has a rare talent, one that in theory is exclusive to Fire Keeper: the ability to "Draw Out True Strength", which is to say he can make the Ashen One stronger. Furthermore, unlike the Fire Keeper or the Emerald Herald, he does not require a cost in souls to do so, and instead brands the Ashen One, the service of whom he can enter, with a Dark Sigil such as the one wore by the Fire Keeper who had entered the Abyss every time, as a way to help prepare the Ashen One\'s ascension as the "Lord of Hollows" to bring about the Age of Dark. title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: In *Scholar of the First Sin*, Aldia, the older brother of King Vendrick, hints at a path for the Bearer of the Curse that differs from the one presented to them. If the conditions are met, he can serve as the final boss of *Dark Souls II*, with his fight triggering after Nashandra's; he, notably, is the only boss in any *Dark Souls* game not to die when defeated, and as such drops no souls nor items, with the player instead gaining the option of an alternate ending in which the Bearer of the Curse is hinted to as following this mysterious other path at Aldia's side. He is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III* via the Soul Stream description, which refers to him as "**the first of the Scholars**". He is voiced by David Gant, who also voiced Oswald of Carim in *Dark Souls*.

title: Herald Armor
snippet:
Herald Armor -  Dark Souls III - armor - lead 
 lead : The **Herald Armor** is a chest armor in *Dark Souls III*. It is part of the Herald Set.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - appearance 
 appearance : In the trailers, artwork, and promotional artwork for *Dark Souls II*, the Bearer of the Curse is depicted wearing the Faraam Set as well as using the Longsword and Spear (dual-wielding) along with the Golden Wing Shield as their main weapons. In the intro video of *Dark Souls II*, the Bearer of the Curse is seen wearing the Imported Set.

In-game, like the Chosen Undead from *Dark Souls*, the Bearer of the Curse's appearance and attributes are determined by the player, including their face/body, sex, origin, starting class and equipment.

Also, like the Chosen Undead, the character's personality is portrayed as an archetypal silent protagonist who doesn't have any sort of spoken dialogue during the game (aside from making some grunts or cries whenever they are hurt or killed).

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
At the bottom of the gaping hole in Majula lurks things long forgotten. Here, The Rotten, a hideous amalgamation of corpses awaits. After making their way through The Gutter, a place where unwanted things have been discarded, the Bearer of the Curse faces down the Rotten itself in its lair, slaying it and claiming its soul for their own.

After freeing Rosabeth of Melfia from her petrification, the path is now open from Majula to Brightstone Cove Tseldora. The Brightstone Cove Tseldora once housed a prosperous town, grown rich after its founder, the Duke Tseldora, discovered its massive crystal deposits. The Duke was always a peculiar figure however, obsessed with spiders, and one day, a massive spider known as The Duke's Dear Freja and her countless children overran the town, and the Duke was never seen again. Fighting their way to the spider's lair, the Bearer of the Curse slays the beast and finds the final Great Soul hidden in her lair.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : While not mentioned in the game, according to the official *Dark Souls II* twitter, the Bearer of the Curse for both genders have birthdates; April 8th for the female character, and May 8th for the male character. This was agreed upon by the developers as it represents them well and is a fun additional fact. This extra information is recent and mentioned on twitter after the game's online servers went online.

title: Drangleic
snippet: In the darkest hour of his reign, Vendrick also realized that his Queen, Nashandra, was a creature of the Abyss, and harbored an insatiable desire for strength. She was a fragment of a dark creature taken a human form, obsessed with the King's powerful soul. Impelled by her cravings, Nashandra sought souls, and strove to make the strength of the Giants her own, everything to reach the Throne of Want and the link for the First Flame so it could spread the Dark. Her painting in the castle was in fact able to curse the undead, making them hollow and draining their life, and only the king knew whether the depiction of the Queen was a resentful mockery, or an affectionate exaltation. At this point Vendrick had achieved a profound understanding of the truths of the world. Stone-humped Hag -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia

In addition she was present in Lothric when Prince Lorian was alive Thus it is possible that she is connected to Emma, the High Priestess of Lothric, or was Emma's precedessor.
The kingdoms and townships referred to are actually part of the Dreg Heap itself: most of the level is comprised of the ruins of Lothric, while there is one area that is visible (but cannot be visited) once the roots of the great tree in the swamp are climbed and the horizon zoomed in: the ruins of the Undead Settlement can be seen in the distance, between two sections of rubble.

title: Dark Ember
snippet:
Dark Ember -  Dark Souls - item - trivia 
 trivia : Despite the description of the Dark Ember claims that the occult weapons are effective against the gods and their kin, neither Gravelord Nito, the daughters of chaos nor their followers are weak to the occult damage. Actually, the only one susceptible to the occult damage are Gwyn, his son Gwyndolin, and their followers. The original description of the Dark Ember says "effective against the clan of the gods and their followers". The only clan of gods ever described is the one guided by Gwyn, which neither Nito or Izalith belonged to, therefore, it's plausible to theorize that the occult weapons are effective specifically against Gwyn, his family, and their followers.

title: Blacksmith Lenigrast
snippet: Despite his dislike of aimless travelers, he will offer his services and advice to his Undead benefactor. He will also be quite glad to see his dear daughter in one piece should she move to Majula, content with keeping an eye from afar, though she, on the other end, doesn't recognize him, possibly due to his Hollowing body. He doesn't seem to notice that her current obliviousness is a result of her loss of memory, as she is likely affected by the Curse herself, though she doesn't show it physically. Lenigrast will also warn the Bearer of the Curse to stay clear of Laddersmith Gilligan whenever he finds his way to the hamlet, as he is quite the well-known scoundrel back in Volgen, often stirring up trouble with his greedy disposition.

title: Elizabeth
snippet:
Elizabeth -  Dark Souls II - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Elizabeth is a member of the Mushroom People of the adjacent woods. She is a master of golden sorcery and the guardian of Oolacile's Sanctuary, as well as Princess Dusk's wet nurse. The two appear to be very close, as the princess will tell her about the Chosen Undead, who rescued her from her imprisonment in the Golden Crystal Golem. She is also adept in medicine, treating mushrooms into potent restorative items.

When the Chosen Undead is dragged into the past by Manus, she is able to instantly recognize them due to the stories of Dusk. She begs for their help and shares her insight and wares with them. She speaks of Knight Artorias, and how he would fall to the Abyss, and of Marvelous Chester, another man from a faraway time who she describes as being odious.

title: Merchant Hag Melentia
snippet: Beneath her crazed facade, the old merchant hides a dark secret. Her hands are permeated by a dark aura which will curse anyone that she touches, making them Hollow almost instantly. It is possible, then, that Melentia is some sort of witch or hexer.

title: Herald (class)
snippet:
Herald (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Herald** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a hybrid class, with a decent amount of Vigor, Strength, Dexterity, and Faith, but a slightly below average Attunement (especially for a class with a starting spell) and Endurance. It seems intended to provide the basis for a build more focused on either one of Strength or Dexterity or a mix of both, that still has the stats to carry some supportive Miracles from its Faith.

Its Spear deals somewhat mediocre damage and is quite short for a polearm, but is actually fairly quick and can attack while still keeping a block up, at the cost of lowering that block's effectiveness (meaning even a 100% block shield will let some damage slip through if hit). Its skill is Shield Splitter, a heavy thrust that partially bypasses blocking.

snippet:
Witch of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : The **Witch of Izalith** or simply **Izalith** (イザリス) is a mentioned character in *Dark Souls*. She is also mentioned in *Dark Souls II*, although by that time her name is lost to history and only her nickname of "mother of pyromancy" remains.

A legendary fire sorcerer who found one of the four Lord Souls, she helped bring an end to the Age of Ancients and the rule of the dragons to establish the Age of Fire, and established an underground civilization named after her. She had many daughters, nicknamed the "Daughters of Chaos", which included Quelaag, Quelana and "The Fair Lady", as well as a son. By the time of the game's events, her magical experiments backfired, fusing her soul and two of her daughters' into a new horrible being, the Bed of Chaos. Although the Bed was eventually slain by the Chosen Undead and its soul fed to the Lordvessel, fragments of the Witch's soul survived.

snippet:
In addition to that, both characters are women, and both of them are connected to the Lost Bastille; the Sinner for being imprisoned in the nearby Sinners' Rise, and the Princess of Venn for building her belfry within the old fort. Sulyvahn would respond to his ally's call, ordering his Dancer to serve as a Boreal Outrider Knight in Lothric alongside a division of Boreal Outrider Knights, under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. title: Nahr Alma, God of Blood
snippet: The deity is associated with scythes, the same tool known to be emblematic of the mistress of the painting, as well as darkness, in a way that is reminiscent of the occult powers sealed away in Ariamis, of which the white crossbreed was permeated. The robes of Nahr Alma's followers are decorated with a white fur collar and bone-like protrusions that resemble wings without membranes. The small connection to magic and the power of the moon that the cult has through the Crescent Sickle could also be explained away by Priscilla's likely descent from Seath, who was likewise tied to the celestial object. Even the prominence of pyromancy among his followers could find an answer in this connection, as Pyromancers, of the Chaos variety specifically, often find their way to the frigid painted landscapes of the forsaken.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - plot 
 plot : Aldia serves as a lore-centric character, alluding to a great deal of things in relation to the lore of *Dark Souls II*.

When the Bearer of the Curse has defeated the Four Great Ones and lit the Primal Bonfires he will emerge and guide the Bearer of the Curse towards his brother Vendrick, now a mindless hollow. He continues to appear to the Bearer of the Curse, seeking to learn their intentions and telling them of the nature of the curse and the fabric of their world.

He will finally attack the Bearer of the Curse before they can take the Throne of Want, seeking to test them. When Aldia is defeated, he will ask what the Bearer of the Curse wants: light, dark or something else entirely. If the Bearer of the Curse chooses to reject the throne and leave, Aldia will narrate the Bearer of the Curse's departure from the throne.

title: Throne of Want
snippet:
Throne of Want -  Dark Souls II - location - plot 
 plot : The Throne of Want is the final location in *Dark Souls II*, where the Bearer of the Curse must best the Throne Watcher and Defender and Nashandra to become a true monarch and claim the Throne. However, if the player has killed Vendrick before Nashandra, Aldia will appear as the final boss.

The Emerald Herald also makes an appearance at the Throne’s entrance where she reveals her true name. In the aftermath, either she or Aldia will narrate the game’s ending.

The area can only be accessed through use of the King's Ring. And the throne itself and only be reached with the Giant's Kinship.

title: Vendrick
snippet:
Vendrick -  Dark Souls II - boss - plot 
 plot : After an untold amount of time in confinement, the King of Drangleic remains a hollowed husk of his former self. The player may choose to spare the king, leaving him to wander eternally, or slay him and end his misery.

Using the Ashen Mist Heart, the Bearer of the Curse may also enter the Memory of the King, where they may interact with King Vendrick as he was before he went hollow. Bitter and grieving his failures, Vendrick tells the Bearer to seek the crowns of old kings of yore. Once they have brought him all the crowns, Vendrick will unlock their power, making the Bearer of the Curse immune to the hollowing effects of the curse. He advises the Bearer of the Curse to seek a third path beyond Light and Dark, echoing his brother.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet: At some point, after Gwyndolin had become the "Chief Deity" of the Anor Londo clan, Yorshka reached Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city her brother had built on the ruins of Anor Londo to house the Irithyllians, hybrids between the race of the gods of Anor Londo and humans. Here she was welcomed by Gwyndolin who formed a relationship of deep affection with his newfound sister, giving her a sacred chime and even the name Yorshka. Eventually a church was built in her name inside Irithyll—exactly where the Painted World of Ariamis was once kept— in which she was venerated as a goddess by the humans who worked in the city.

 proceed_to_throne : After the player defeats Nashandra (or Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin, if his conditions are met) at the Throne of Want, a cutscene will play showing the player walking atop the golems, who create a bridge for the player to cross, and into a throne room. In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse will accept their part in the cycle of the world and take the throne. Doing so means that they will either sacrifice themselves to link the flame, or allow the flame to continue to fade and become the Dark Lord. Which the Bearer of the Curse chooses is known only to them.

The original Japanese item description reads: "There is a throne fitting for each king. The view from the throne is known only to the one who sits upon it. Or does the throne show he who sits upon it what they want to see?".

title: Captain Drummond
snippet: What happened to Drummond afterwards is never stated, but his armor, sword and shield can be found in the ruins of the fort, now enveloped by the surrounding forest, around the wall where the Giant Lord was felled in the past. It is therefore likely that he perished shortly after the victory on the Giants, becoming the last of his family line. The absence of his helm is also meaningful, as he gifted it to the Bearer of the Curse in the past for helping his remaining army in their hour of need.

title: Rosabeth of Melfia
snippet:
Thankfully for her, the Bearer of the Curse would find and release her from her horrible state with a Fragrant Branch of Yore. She will be extremely grateful for their help, though greatly embarrassed due to the state of her attire. After a change of clothing provided by her benefactor, she'll move to Majula, in hopes of meeting up with her teacher there. She will begin to wonder if Carhillion hadn't simply ditched her after she first lost track of him, though in truth the old master hoped she was safe and wondered where she disappeared to.

Even should they reunite in Majula, Rosabeth will decide to practice on her own, wishing to see what she can achieve by herself.

No negative effects come from attempting to kill her, she will still talk to you and sell you things. An unused dialogue quote found in the game's files, states it was possible to kill Shalquoir.

title: Crestfallen Saulden
snippet:
Crestfallen Saulden -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Saulden is a cursed Undead, much like the Bearer of the Curse and many who have found their way in Drangleic. Like them, he was expected to go on a perilous journey to find a way to end the Curse, but lost hope along the way, his spirit crushed by the trials of the ruined kingdom. As a result, he sits at the foot of the great monument of Majula, deep in contemplation, and he offers guidance to those who find their way to the seaside hamlet. He thinks it's hopeless to look for a cure for the Curse, since it originates from life and the soul itself.

snippet:

During her second encounter, Lucatiel will tell the player about her past in Mirrah. She will then take off her mask, revealing her partly hollowed visage, and give the player a Human Effigy, while claiming not to even know what it is.

The third time she is met, she tells the player about her fears of losing her memories and of her brother. Lucatiel will explain how he is a better swordsman than her and she confesses that her brother, who is another victim of the curse of undeath, might be in Drangleic. She then gifts the Ring of Steel Protection +1.

snippet: Following the destruction of the Bed of Chaos, Quelana appears to have returned to Izalith, or what remains of it, at some point. title: Flame of Chaos
snippet:
Flame of Chaos -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Flame of Chaos was created by the Witch of Izalith when she attempted to use her Lord Soul to recreate the First Flame. When she was unable to control it, she was consumed by it and transformed into the Bed of Chaos, mother of all Demons. Most of her children were similarly consumed and transformed into monstrosities; her daughter Quelana, however, escaped and used the Flame of Chaos to create the art of Pyromancy.

After the defeat of the Bed of Chaos at the hand of the Chosen Undead, the flames of Chaos persisted. It would eventually be discovered beneath Eleum Loyce, in the form of The Old Chaos. The Old Chaos would go on to consume many of Eleum Loyce's knights, turning them into Charred Loyce Knights, and eventually claiming the ruler of Eleum Loyce himself. The Ivory King would eventually be freed, at the bequest of his oracle Alsanna, by the Bearer of the Curse.

Eventually, the Witch of Izalith attempted to duplicate the First Flame. What she instead produced was a twisted being of chaotic fire: the Bed of Chaos, source of all demons. Several of the Witch's daughters were transformed into chaos demons, and her son became the monstrous Ceaseless Discharge.

snippet: He set up shop in a vacant house in Majula, taking all of his equipment inside to begin work right away. snippet: The Lord of Sunlight would end up gifting the Pygmies with a magnificent city at the edge of the world, sealing the deal by relinquishing his beloved daughter too, who would remain there until the day he would return for her. Shira and her trusted friend, the dragon Midir, who was raised by the Gods and given the duty of battling the Dark, would follow their liege and guard the Ringed City, keeping those who would rouse her awake at bay. By the king's decree, the Judicator Giants and the Spears of the Church would follow suit, ensuring peace. Shira seemes to admire this order, especially those of them who would reach the rank of Divine Spear.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: While the Giants invasion was largely stopped, their souls remained powerful. King Vendrick's elder brother, Lord Aldia, kept Giants in his manor and performed experiments on them in an attempt to recreate a dragon. The outcome of Lord Aldia's experiments is unknown, but oddly when the Ancient Dragon roosting at the summit of Aldia's realm was slain, the soul of a Giant was found in its remains. Legend holds that the Giants' resentment of King Vendrick was possibly emboldened in death. This was proven true when the Bearer of the Curse fought the hollowed remains of Vendrick. With the souls of several Giants in the Bearer's possession, Vendrick was significantly weakened and subsequently defeated.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
All of her attacks inflict Curse Build-up.

For melee characters it is also possible to equip light armor and dodge her attacks, ignoring the Curse buildup and only healing when your health starts draining. snippet: Alsanna, as the heiress to her Lord's wishes and in reverence of the apocalypse, devoted herself and the power of her Dark Soul to a ritual in the hopes of appeasing the raging flame. With the ivory gates opened, the land of Eleum Loyce grew cold and lifeless, turning into a frigid expanse, in an attempt to freeze Chaos along with the entire country. The remaining Knights of Eleum Loyce remained to watch over the Garrison Ward under the King's final orders to contain the Chaos, waiting patiently for a new leader strong enough to guide them into its depths, while Alsanna remained in prayer inside the Cathedral over the depths to continue the ritual. The Old Chaos was thus contained, albeit it corrupted the Ivory King and his knights, nevertheless remaining confined by Alsanna's tireless effort. Chaos was repressed until a Bearer of the Curse came along and destroyed the Burnt King and his corrupted Eleum Loyce knights, definitively eradicating the offshoots of Chaos from Drangleic.

snippet: Left to his own devices after his brother's failure to grant humans the immortality of dragons, Vendrick desperately sought to purge the curse of Undeath that was slowly devouring his kingdom. One of these experiments was conducted on the Milfanito, creatures conceived by Gravelord Nito to keep Undead under control. Coalescing again, this abyss expanded across the region and assimilated all things into its growth, with its darkness felt even by those attuned to magic in neighbouring regions. A group of Undead led by Darkdiver Grandahl, called the Pilgrims of Dark, started to make pilgrimages to what they considered holy sites and delved into the Dark Chasm, to overcome the trials that lurked in the depths to refine the darkness within them. In the heart of the abyss, the Darklurker manifested: A dark, angelic creature that manipulated darkness along with sorcery, pyromancy and miracles and demonstrated superhuman abilities.

title: Drangleic

Drangleic Sword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Greatsword of Drummond, Royal Army Captain. An old and unadorned sword, perhaps, but the pride and joy of this venerable captain.

An heirloom passed from grandfather to father, and then from father to son. Drummond, and those before him, used this sword to repel those who would threaten their great land.

title: Raulmond, Knight of Drangleic
snippet:
Raulmond, Knight of Drangleic -  Dark Souls II - character - theories 
 theories : It's possible that Raulmond is related to Captain Drummond, a warrior of Drangleic whose family has been defending the fort for generations, something Raulmond had done in the past too, until his death. The knight could have been Drummond's father or even grandfather, as both had fought the invading Giants according to the current captain, and might have died during the struggle. The names of the two soldiers are also remarkably similar, which would make a lot of sense if they were related in some way.

title: Raulmond, Knight of Drangleic
snippet:
Raulmond, Knight of Drangleic -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Raulmond was a knight who served King Vendrick in his time, acting as a guardian of his fort until his own demise. He was known for cershing rings that bore the protection of dragons throughout all of his life and service to Drangleic. He might have been an exceptional champion, however, as the first of his rings is the second highest reward of the Company of Champions covenant, a group of brave warriors based in Majula who scoff at danger and seek greater challenges, their names engraved to commemorate their deeds.
